External Access Registry

            
Manage external resources — APIs, databases, MCP servers, cloud services

        

        

            
            
            
        

    


    
    

        

            
📖 External Access Registry — Quick Guide

            
        

        
What is this? The External Access Registry defines every external system your agents can interact with — APIs, databases, MCP servers, cloud services. The entitlement layer uses this registry to control which users/skills can access which external resources.

        

            

                
Form View

                
    
                    
  • Click "+ Add Resource" to create a new entry
    • 
                    
  • Set the ID (must start with external:)
    • 
                    
  • Choose Type — fields adapt automatically (http shows hosts/paths/methods, db shows databases, mcp shows connections)
    • 
                    
  • Set Risk level (low/medium/high) for audit visibility
    • 
                    
  • Link Credentials and Tools the resource needs
    • 
                    
  • Click "💾 Save" — validates before saving
    • 
                

            

            

                
YAML View

                
    
                    
  • Edit the raw external_access.yaml directly
    • 
                    
  • Click "✓ Validate" to check for errors before saving
    • 
                    
  • Useful for bulk edits, copy-paste, or advanced fields
    • 
                

            

        

        
💡 Tip: Resources are referenced in policies.yaml entitlement rules as external:* patterns. After adding a resource here, grant access to it via the Policies editor.

Credential Manager

            
Add your own encrypted credentials and reference any listed credential in your skills — you can edit the ones you created; contact the creator for others (secrets never leave the server)

        

        

            
            
            
        

    


    
    

        

            
📖 Credential Manager — Quick Guide

            
        

        
What is this? Credentials store API keys, tokens, and passwords that agents use to call external services. All secret values are encrypted at rest with AES-256 (Fernet) and never returned in API responses.

        

            

                
Adding a Credential

                
    
                    
  • Click "+ Add Credential"
    • 
                    
  • Enter a Name (used in external_access.yaml and SKILL.md)
    • 
                    
  • Choose Type: bearer (token), api_key (key), or basic (username + password)
    • 
                    
  • Enter the secret value — it will be encrypted on save
    • 
                    
  • Scope restricts which skills can use it (empty = all skills)
    • 
                    
  • TTL sets cache duration in seconds (optional)
    • 
                

            

            

                
How It Works

                
    
                    
  • Agents reference credentials as $CRED_name in curl/API calls
    • 
                    
  • The kernel resolves and injects the real value at runtime — the LLM never sees secrets
    • 
                    
  • Link credentials to resources in the External Access panel
    • 
                    
  • YAML view shows masked values (read-only) for audit purposes
    • 
                

            

        

        
🔐 Security: Deleting a credential is permanent. Any agent or resource referencing it will fail until a replacement is created with the same name.

    


    
    


    
    

        
⚠ Read-only — secret values are masked. Use Form view to edit credentials.

        

    


    
    

        
        

            🔑 Credentials are shared — anyone can reference them in skills. You can add your own and edit the ones you created; for credentials created by others, contact the listed creator.
        

        
        

            👁 View only — you can reference these credential names in your skills. Contact a developer or admin to add or modify credentials.

Entitlement Policies

            
Manage tenant entitlement rules — who can access what resources

        

        

            
            
        

    


    
    

        

            
📖 Entitlement Policies — Quick Guide

            
        

        
What is this? Policies define who can access which resources. Each policy has a principal match (roles/groups), an effect (allow/deny), actions (use/read/write/manage), and target resources (skills, tools, agents, external, etc.).

        

            

                
Form View

                
    
                    
  • Click "+ Add Policy" to create a new rule
    • 
                    
  • Set a unique ID (e.g., finance-ar-skill-access)
    • 
                    
  • Toggle Effect between allow (green) and deny (red)
    • 
                    
  • Roles/Groups — select principals from the dropdown lists
    • 
                    
  • Actions — pick from the dropdown (definitions listed below)
    • 
                    
  • Resources — pick a type (Skills, Tools, Agents, MCP, …), then choose type:* or a specific item
    • 
                

            

            

                
YAML View

                
    
                    
  • Edit the raw policies.yaml directly
    • 
                    
  • Click "✓ Validate" before saving
    • 
                    
  • Useful for bulk edits, copy-paste, or advanced conditions
    • 
                

            

        

        

            
Action definitions

            
Each action is checked by enforce_entitlement() before the matching API or runtime operation proceeds. Default is deny if no policy grants the action.

            

                
            

        

        
💡 Tip: After editing, use the Access Simulator tab to test your changes before they affect live users.

Access Simulator

            
Test whether a principal is allowed or denied for a specific action + resource

        

        

            
        

    


    
    

        

            
📖 Access Simulator — Quick Guide

            
        

        
What is this? The Access Simulator lets you test a single entitlement decision without actually executing anything. Enter a principal (who), an action (what), and a resource (which), then see if the current policies allow or deny it.

        

            

                
Principal Fields

                
    
                    
  • Role — required (one per user, same as login)
    • 
                    
  • User ID / Email — optional; pick email to auto-fill from roster
    • 
                    
  • Groups — optional; multiple allowed (same as user account groups)
    • 
                

            

            

                
Resource Fields

                
    
                    
  • Action — pick from the dropdown (definitions listed below)
    • 
                    
  • Resource Type — skill, agent, tool, context, external, mcp
    • 
                    
  • Resource ID — the specific resource name (e.g., my_skill)
    • 
                

            

        

        

            
Action definitions

            
Each action is checked by enforce_entitlement() before the matching API or runtime operation proceeds. Default is deny if no policy grants the action.

            

                
            

        

        
💡 Tip: The result shows the matched policy name and reason, so you can quickly debug unexpected denials.

Effective Access Matrix

            
View the full access matrix for a principal across all resource types

        

        

            
        

    


    
    

        

            
📖 Effective Access Matrix — Quick Guide

            
        

        
What is this? The Effective Access Matrix evaluates all policies for a given principal and shows which resources are allowed or denied across every resource type (skills, agents, tools, contexts, external, databases, MCP connections).

        

            

                
How to Use

                
    
                    
  • Set role (required) and optional groups — matches how login identity is built
    • 
                    
  • Click "Load Matrix"
    • 
                    
  • See a summary grid of allowed/denied counts per resource type
    • 
                    
  • Click any resource type card to expand the detailed list
    • 
                

            

            

                
Reading the Results

                
    
                    
  • Green count = allowed resources, Red = denied
    • 
                    
  • Expanded view shows each resource with its allowed actions
    • 
                    
  • Use this to audit a user's total access footprint
    • 
                

            

        

        
🔐 Security: This evaluates against live tenant policies + real resource inventories. Changes to policies are reflected immediately.

Users & Access

            
Every user and what they can reach across each resource type — one consolidated view

        

        

            
            
        

    


    
    

        

            
📖 Users & Access — Quick Guide

            
        

        
What is this? A consolidated roster of every user joined with their effective access. Each cell shows allowed / total for that resource type. Click a row to see exactly which skills, tools, contexts, etc. each user can reach and why.

        

            

                
Where the data comes from

                
    
                    
  • Roster: GET /auth/users (email, role, status)
    • 
                    
  • Access: POST /api/security/effective-access per user
    • 
                    
  • Evaluated live against current tenant policies
    • 
                

            

            

                
Notes

                
    
                    
  • Access is computed from each user's role; group-scoped grants resolve from the login token, not this roster
    • 
                    
  • Provider-agnostic — swap to Entra/Okta/Google SSO and only the roster source changes
    • 
                    
  • Click a row → drawer; use "Open in Simulator" for what-if tests
    • 
                

            

        

    


    

        
        

            
            
            
            
            Provider:  · Tenant: company
        


        
        

            ● active
            ○ suspended/locked
            n/n allowed / total

Lifecycle Hooks

            
Author governance hooks (e.g. a blocking PreToolUse → HITL gate) — saved to the agent's config.yaml

        

        

            
            
            
            
            
        

    


    
    

        

            
📖 Lifecycle Hooks — Quick Guide

            
        

        
A hook runs your code at a lifecycle point (e.g. before a tool call). A blocking PreToolUse hook with fail_policy: closed is the deterministic way to force HITL: when it blocks, the call becomes a pending approval and shows up in the same Approve/Deny flow your workstreams use.

        
    
            
  • Add blocking PreToolUse (HITL) fills a ready-to-use HITL template — set the matcher (tool name) and command.
    • 
            
  • Saving rewrites only the hooks: section of config.yaml and reloads the agent — no restart.
    • 
            
  • For simple "ask before X" rules, prefer a skill's approval_rules; use hooks when you need a code-level guarantee.
    • 
        


        

            
All  events, by category

            

                
            

        

    


    

        
        

            ● Hooks ENABLED
            ● Hooks DISABLED — saved hooks will NOT run (CAPABILITY_HOOKS_ENABLED=false)

Entitlement Audit Log

            
Filterable log of entitlement decisions — who accessed what and when

        

        

            
            
        

    


    
    

        

            
📖 Audit Log — Quick Guide

            
        

        
What is this? Every entitlement decision (allowed or denied) is logged. This panel lets you search and filter those events to investigate access patterns, debug policy issues, or audit compliance.

        

            

                
Filters

                
    
                    
  • User / Email — pick a user from the dropdown to filter events
    • 
                    
  • Action — partial match (use, read, manage, etc.)
    • 
                    
  • Resource — partial match on resource key
    • 
                    
  • Denied only — toggle to show only denied events
    • 
                

            

            

                
Event Details

                
    
                    
  • Each row shows: user, timestamp, action → resource, allow/deny
    • 
                    
  • Matched policy + reason shown for debugging
    • 
                    
  • Events come from both entitlements + external access audit logs
    • 
                    
  • Sorted newest first, limited to 200 events
    • 
                

            

        

        
🔍 Tip: To investigate a specific denial, filter by user ID and toggle "Denied only". The matched policy tells you exactly which rule caused it.

🕸 Graph Studio

                        
Browse, author, and run process-graph skills (DAGs of skill-nodes with verifiers & convergence).

                    

                    
                    
                    
                

                

                    
                    

                        
                    

                

            


            
            

                
                

                    
                    
                    
                    
                    
                    
                    
                


                

                    
                    

                        
                        

                            
✨ Draft with AI

                            
                            

                                
                                Generates a graph you can then edit below.
                            

                            
                        


                        
                        

                            Template:
                            
                            
                        

                        

                            Nodes: each has id, skill (existing skill), role (worker/verifier), task. A verifier reviews upstream results and replies with its verdict.pass_when word (e.g. PASS).

                            Edges: from → to. A when: pass/fail edge must start at a verifier. Reference upstream output with {{node.result}} in a task.

                            Convergence: loop the scope until the verifier passes, up to max loops, then on_exhausted (escalate/stop). Grounding: an independent verifier can't reuse a node's own skill.
